steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: German has four cases that show the role of a noun in a sentence. Each case affects the articles (der/die/das), adjectives and pronouns. | Exam Tip: Two-way prepositions: movement towards = ACCUSATIVE (Wohin?); location/position = DATIVE (Wo?). "Ich gehe in die Stadt" (acc — movement) vs "Ich bin in der Stadt" (dat — location). | German Exam Tips — Cases: Nominative, Accusative, Dative and Genitive: 1. For Cases: Nominative, Accusative, Dative and Genitive, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4.
